document.title: BoulderMe: your build guide
document.summary: Build a welcoming iOS app that helps people find a climbing partner at their gym. Follow these steps to set up Supabase, implement private invitations and prove the first release works.

decisions.question: Should chat ship in the first release?
decisions.recommendation: Start with invitations and defer open chat until moderation is ready.
decisions.reason: This keeps the first complete workflow small while preserving consent and privacy.

services.purpose: Authentication and a private database for climbers and invitations.
services.setup: Create development and production projects in an account you own. Verify current plan limits first.
services.publicConfig: SUPABASE_URL and SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY belong in client configuration.
services.secretConfig: SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY is server-only. Enter its real value in provider secrets, never in chat.
services.costNotes: Review current pricing and forecast database, file and active-user usage before launch.

steps.title: Choose the first release
instructions: Confirm the iOS target, initial gyms and adult audience.
Review profile visibility and decide whether chat is deferred.
Write the chosen defaults into the project brief.
steps.doneWhen: The brief records the launch scope and visibility rules.
steps.ifBlocked: If a decision is unclear, ask the coding AI for one recommended default.

steps.title: Prepare your tools
instructions: Open Apple developer resources on your Mac.
Install the supported Xcode release after verifying system requirements.
Create a new local project folder for BoulderMe.
steps.doneWhen: An empty app runs in the iOS simulator.
steps.ifBlocked: If the simulator fails, check Xcode platform downloads and selected device.

steps.title: Create Supabase projects
instructions: Open the official Supabase getting-started guide.
Create a development project in your own account and keep its database password local.
Record the project URL and publishable key in local configuration.
steps.doneWhen: The app can reach the selected development project.
steps.ifBlocked: If the request fails, confirm the project URL and network connection.

steps.title: Build the database
instructions: Create versioned migrations for profiles, gyms and invitations.
Add foreign keys, status checks, indexes and RLS policies.
Apply migrations locally and insert synthetic seed data.
steps.doneWhen: A fresh local database can be rebuilt from migrations.
steps.ifBlocked: If a migration fails, inspect the first error and repair it before proceeding.

steps.title: Connect sign-in
instructions: Enable the selected email sign-in method in development.
Configure app callbacks using the actual app identifier.
Test sign-in, sign-out, recovery and an expired session.
steps.doneWhen: A verified test account can sign in again after restarting the app.
steps.ifBlocked: If callback handling fails, compare the app URL with the configured allowed redirect.

steps.title: Find partners
instructions: Build the gym picker and skill filters using synthetic profiles.
Fetch only discoverable profiles with pagination.
Add empty, loading, offline and retry states.
steps.doneWhen: Changing gym or skill changes the visible partner results.
steps.ifBlocked: If no results appear, verify seed data and test the same query as the signed-in user.

steps.title: Complete invitations
instructions: Implement pending, accepted, declined, cancelled and expired states.
Authorize and lock state transitions on the server.
Connect the invitation controls and show recoverable errors.
steps.doneWhen: Two accounts can complete the invitation workflow without duplicate records.
steps.ifBlocked: If acceptance fails, check the actor, current state and transaction result.

steps.title: Run acceptance checks
instructions: Run unit tests and server permission tests.
Exercise the app on a real device with unrelated test accounts.
Record real provider checks separately from mocked tests.
steps.doneWhen: The acceptance table has passing evidence for every launch requirement.
steps.ifBlocked: If a test fails, resolve the underlying behavior and rerun the affected checks.

steps.title: Prepare release
instructions: Apply migrations and configure callbacks in staging first.
Prepare support and privacy materials and verify current store requirements.
Review costs and request a separate publishing decision.
steps.doneWhen: The staging checklist is complete and the owner has reviewed the release.
steps.ifBlocked: If a provider is not configured, keep the release blocked and record the missing setup.

steps.title: Maintain your app
instructions: Document daily health checks and weekly cost review.
Restore a staging backup and compare expected records.
Write rollback, secret rotation and user deletion instructions.
steps.doneWhen: Another operator can follow the handover to run and recover the app.
steps.ifBlocked: If restoration fails, fix the procedure and repeat it before relying on the backup.

items.title: First release
items.detail: Launch an iOS app for adults to find climbing partners at selected gyms, with profiles, filters and consent-based invitations.

items.title: Later releases
items.detail: Defer paid cosmetics and open messaging until invitation privacy and report handling have passed real-device acceptance tests.

items.title: Success
items.detail: Two unrelated test accounts can complete a session invitation while a third account cannot inspect their private invitation.

items.title: Client
items.detail: SwiftUI presents profiles and session state. The server authorizes every write; sample prototype screens never call Supabase.

items.title: Backend
items.detail: Supabase provides Auth and Postgres. Use a versioned migration folder and separate development and production projects.

items.title: Milestones
items.detail: Build a local shell, a persisted invitation workflow, authentication, denial tests and staging before considering a public release.

items.title: Profiles
items.detail: profiles: id uuid references auth.users, display_name text, gym_id uuid, skill_level integer. Only owners can change their profile.

items.title: Invitations
items.detail: invitations: id uuid primary key, sender_id and recipient_id uuid, status text, starts_at timestamptz. Reject self-invitations.

items.title: Constraints
items.detail: Add foreign keys and a uniqueness rule for an active invitation between a pair and session. Index recipient_id and starts_at.

items.title: Anonymous
items.detail: Anonymous visitors cannot read profiles, memberships or invitations. Authentication alone never grants administrative permissions.

items.title: Members
items.detail: Members can read discoverable profiles and their own invitations. An unrelated third user must receive no private invitation rows.

items.title: Privileged writes
items.detail: Use a server-authorized transaction to accept an invitation. Do not expose the Supabase service role key to the iOS client.

items.title: Find a partner
items.detail: A member chooses a gym and skill range. Filter on the server, paginate stable results, and provide loading, empty and retry states.

items.title: Invite and accept
items.detail: Invitation states are pending, accepted, declined, cancelled and expired. Only the recipient may accept a pending invitation.

items.title: Concurrency
items.detail: Lock the pending invitation before transitioning its state. Repeated accepts return the same result; a cancellation race has one winner.

items.title: Privacy
items.detail: Use a chosen gym instead of exact live location. Document visibility and retention before asking the owner to approve launch.

items.title: Abuse
items.detail: Rate limit invitations and enforce blocking in both reads and server writes. Reports must reach an operator with a review process.

items.title: Secrets
items.detail: Use placeholder-only environment examples. Keep credentials out of source, logs and screenshots; test least-privilege access.

items.title: Happy path
items.detail: Use two synthetic accounts to create profiles, filter climbers, send an invitation and accept it from the recipient account.

items.title: Denied access
items.detail: Try accepting as the sender and reading as an unrelated third account. Both operations must be rejected by the backend.

items.title: Recovery
items.detail: Repeat the acceptance request, simulate a dropped response, and verify one accepted record. Restore a staging backup and compare counts.

items.title: Owner accounts
items.detail: The owner completes Apple enrollment and Supabase account setup. Verify current account fees and distribution prerequisites.

items.title: Staging gate
items.detail: Apply migrations in staging and run real-device acceptance checks with synthetic users. Record evidence and remaining blockers.

items.title: Approved rollout
items.detail: After separate publishing approval, back up data, apply compatible migrations, release gradually and verify health and sign-in.

items.title: Daily and weekly
items.detail: Check authentication failures and invitation errors daily. Review support reports, storage growth and provider costs every week.

items.title: Restore and rotation
items.detail: Test a staging backup restore monthly. Rotate exposed keys promptly and revoke affected sessions without logging secret values.

items.title: Handover
items.detail: Deliver README, SETUP, SERVICES, OPERATIONS and FOLLOW_UP_PROMPTS with runnable commands, tested release steps and known limitations.

featureCoverage.behavior: Choose a gym and skill range to find visible profiles that match the selected filters.
featureCoverage.verification: Changing the selected gym hides profiles from other gyms and preserves pagination.

featureCoverage.behavior: Invite another climber, then accept from the recipient account through an authorized transition.
featureCoverage.verification: A recipient can accept once; the sender and unrelated users cannot accept on their behalf.
